name: Prompt chaining
description: Break a task into a sequence of LLM calls where each step's output feeds the next, with optional checks in between.
when_it_works_well: Best when a task decomposes cleanly into fixed, sequential subtasks -- trades some latency for higher accuracy on each step.

name: Routing
description: Classify an input and direct it to a specialized prompt, model, or downstream flow rather than handling every case with one generic path.
when_it_works_well: Best for complex tasks with distinct categories that are better handled separately, and when classification can be done reliably.

name: Parallelization
description: Run multiple LLM calls simultaneously on subtasks or perspectives, then aggregate the results (sectioning or voting).
when_it_works_well: Best when subtasks can run independently for speed, or when running the same task multiple times and combining outputs improves confidence.

name: Orchestrator-workers
description: A central LLM dynamically breaks a task into subtasks, delegates them to worker LLM calls, and synthesizes the results.
when_it_works_well: Best for complex, open-ended tasks where the subtasks can't be predicted in advance -- e.g. coding changes that touch an unknown set of files.

name: Evaluator-optimizer
description: One LLM call generates a response while a second evaluates it against explicit criteria and feeds back for another iteration.
when_it_works_well: Best when there are clear evaluation criteria and iterative refinement measurably improves the output, similar to a human editor's revision cycle.

name: Autonomous agent loop
description: The LLM plans, acts via tool calls, observes the result, and repeats -- operating independently until the task is complete or a stopping condition is hit, rather than following a fixed predefined path.
when_it_works_well: Best for open-ended problems where the number of steps can't be predicted and rigid, hardcoded logic would be too brittle -- at the cost that more autonomy also means more cost and more room for compounding errors.

name: ReAct (Reason + Act)
description: Interleaves explicit reasoning traces with tool-call actions and their observations, so the model 'thinks out loud' about what to do next before each action.
when_it_works_well: The foundational pattern behind most modern tool-using agents; works well whenever a tool's output needs to inform the next reasoning step rather than being used blind.

name: Reflection & self-critique
description: The agent reviews its own prior output or action against the goal (or explicit criteria) and revises before finalizing.
when_it_works_well: Helps catch a model's own mistakes without external supervision, particularly for tasks with a checkable/testable outcome such as code that can be run and tested.

name: Multi-agent collaboration
description: Multiple specialized agents, each with a distinct role, prompt, or tool access, communicate to jointly complete a task, sometimes with one agent acting as coordinator.
when_it_works_well: Best when a task naturally splits into distinct specialist roles (e.g. researcher + writer, or coder + reviewer) and the overhead of agent-to-agent communication is worth the specialization.

name: Human-in-the-loop approval gates
description: The agent proposes an action -- a file edit, a shell command, a commit -- and pauses for explicit human approval before executing it, rather than acting fully autonomously.
when_it_works_well: Best for higher-stakes or hard-to-reverse actions, or whenever trust in the agent's judgment is still being established.
